title: Push-forward of normal currents by maps Lipschitz near the support: existence, uniqueness, mass, support, boundary and linearity (Simon 2.28–2.29; supplied Part 5)
statement: D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q (ℝ^p = Eucl p), M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary. For g : ℝ^p → ℝ^q, ω ∈ D^j(ℝ^q), η ∈ D^j(ℝ^p) and A ⊆ ℝ^p, 'η is compatible with (g, ω) near A' means: there is an open N ⊇ A with η(x) = ω(g(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ g x) for all x ∈ N. For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}), LipPF(X, G, S) means: for every sequence (G_n) of C^∞ maps ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)), every open O ⊇ spt X and every L ∈ ℝ such that eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O, and G_n → G uniformly on O, and for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence (η_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that eventually η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, the sequence X(η_n) converges to S(ω). (I) For all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ such that M(∂Y) < ∞ for every j ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and r > 0 such that G is Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X) and G⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact for every compact K: there is S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S) such that every S′ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S′) equals S, M(S) ≤ Λ^k·M(X) (in ℝ≥0∞) and spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)). (II) For all m, m′, j ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞, G, Λ, r as in (I) (Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X), proper on spt X) and S ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S): LipPF(∂X, G, ∂S). (III) For all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X, X₁, X₂ ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r > 0, S, S₁, S₂ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) and a, a₁ ∈ ℝ such that G is Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X ∪ spt X₁), G⁻¹(K) ∩ (spt X ∪ spt X₁) is compact for every compact K, X₂(ω) = a·X(ω) + a₁·X₁(ω) for all ω, and LipPF(X, G, S), LipPF(X₁, G, S₁), LipPF(X₂, G, S₂): S₂(ω) = a·S(ω) + a₁·S₁(ω) for all ω.
